title.en: The Gnomon of the Zhou: Shang Gao and Chen Zi

author.dates: Western Han, compiled c. 1st century BCE

year_display.zh: 约成书于公元前 1 世纪

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource: Book One, Part One complete, and Part Two up to the point where Chen Zi begins his technical account of the gnomon.
edition.zh: 据中文维基文库：卷上之一全文；卷上之二至陈子开始讲解立竿测影之术处为止。

basis.en: Classical Chinese text of the Han dynasty, about two thousand years old.
basis.zh: 汉代典籍，距今约两千年。

note.en: One of the oldest Chinese books of mathematics and astronomy opens with a conversation about where number comes from, and within a few lines reaches the three-four-five triangle, the gougu relation that Euclid proves as I.47 on the same shelf. Here it is shown rather than proved, with a bent carpenter's square and a ring of squares on a board. The second dialogue is about learning itself: a student fails twice, is sent home to think, and is told that understanding means carrying one case across to many.
note.zh: 这部中国最古老的数学与天文著作之一，以一场关于“数从何而来”的对话开篇，没几行就讲到勾三股四弦五，也就是同一架上欧几里得在卷一命题四十七中证明的那个关系。这里它不是被证明，而是被演示出来的：折一把矩尺，在一块板上把方环绕起来。第二段对话谈的是学习本身：学生两次想不出来，被打发回家去想，老师告诉他，懂就是能把一类事推到万事。

excerpt.orig: 故折矩，以為句廣三，股修四，徑隅五。
excerpt.en: So bend a carpenter's square, making the base three across and the upright four long; then the diagonal between the corners is five.
excerpt.zh: 故折矩，以为句广三，股修四，径隅五。
